hero_description: Vice President (Technical) · RUET Cyber Security Club
about:
I’m Arittro Sarkar, a 4th-year Computer Science student at Rajshahi University of Engineering & Technology (RUET) with a strong interest in cybersecurity and offensive security research. I actively participate in Capture The Flag (CTF) competitions under the handle Devil@32, where I work on challenges involving web security, cryptography, reverse engineering, and exploitation. These experiences have strengthened my ability to analyze complex systems, think critically under pressure, and collaborate effectively in team-based problem-solving environments.

I currently serve as Vice President (Technical) of the RUET Cyber Security Club, where I contribute to leading technical initiatives, organizing hands-on workshops, and guiding members through practical security exercises and CTF-style learning. Through this role, I aim to build a strong technical foundation within the community and encourage a mindset focused on curiosity, experimentation, and ethical security research.

My interest in security is driven by understanding how and why systems break. Rather than viewing vulnerabilities as isolated mistakes, I focus on uncovering flawed assumptions, broken trust models, and weaknesses in system design or implementation. I place a strong emphasis on responsible disclosure and on learning from each finding by tracing issues back to their root causes, which helps me develop a deeper understanding of secure system architecture.

Alongside cybersecurity, I have a solid background in web development, working with technologies such as HTML, CSS, JavaScript, Node.js, Express.js, MongoDB, and React. I believe that strong development knowledge is essential for effective security research. This dual perspective allows me to think like both a builder and an attacker, enabling me to design, analyze, and test applications with security in mind.

I am constantly learning and refining my skills through CTF competitions, bug bounty practice, technical leadership within my club, and personal security projects. My long-term goal is to grow into a skilled security professional who contributes to building more robust systems and a safer, more secure internet.
